title: Come, Kingdom of Our God
description: Come, Kingdom of Our God in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Johns wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 584, “The Kingdom of Love”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, king-dom of our God, Sweet reign of light and love! Shed peace, and hope, and joy a-broad, And wis-dom from a-bove.

lines: Sweet reign of light and love!
Shed peace, and hope, and joy abroad,
There raise and quench the sacred thirst,
And make the broad earth thine;
Stretch o'er her lands and isles the rod
Soon may all tribes be blest
With fruit from life's glad tree;
And in its shade like brothers rest,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Johns died in 1847.
credits: Words by John Johns (1801–1847), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
